description:
MATERIAL. Every one of the twelve is built from exactly one primitive: the square (or a slightly sheared quadrilateral), drawn flat, hard-edged, with no stroke and no texture, at many sizes and many rotations. There is no line work, no curve, no gradient except what accumulates where translucent squares overlap. The ground is a near-black charcoal with a faint blue-green cast, the same in every tile. The drawing colours are a bone/ivory cream, a short ladder of neutral greys from dark slate to near-white, and one chromatic accent: a muted sea-green / verdigris teal. Nothing else. Many of the squares are semi-transparent, so overlaps read as lighter or milkier patches and the pile-ups build soft polygonal haloes.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Two things happening at once in the same frame. In the middle, a rosette: dozens of squares rotated in equal steps about the centre so they lock into a mandala, a snowflake, a compass rose, a cut-paper doily. The symmetry order looks like five to eight depending on seed - 1243682 and 1835793 read as six-pointed stars, 1310661 and 1475115 as broad seven- or eight-lobed discs. Around and behind it, a scattered field of larger opaque squares, each tilted a few degrees off axis, drifting outward like ash, confetti, or tiles knocked off a mosaic, cropped hard by the frame. So: an ordered centre and a disordered surround. A ceremonial object and its debris. That contrast is the idea of the piece and it is legible in all twelve.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Ground colour, palette, the square-only vocabulary, radial symmetry at the centre, a scatter ring outside it, centred composition, and edge bleed - squares are cut in half by the frame on nearly every tile. Anyone would call these one project on sight.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Almost entirely by INK DENSITY and by the cream-to-teal ratio, and the range on that one axis is enormous. 1991107 is nearly solid cream edge to edge with a dark keyhole punched in the middle holding teal chips - figure and ground inverted relative to everything else. 1985692 is a huge pale flower filling the frame with only a dusting of teal specks, very low contrast. 1446330 is the opposite extreme: an almost empty black field with a few small grey squares and a barely-visible dark teal freckle at centre; it is the only tile with essentially no rosette. 1561509 is nearly as sparse - a small pale cluster and a spray of teal chips on black. At the dense-and-graphic end, 1310661 is a solid teal heptagon inside a cream halo, and 1475115 is a bold teal star broken by a cream ring; those two are the strongest images here. In the middle sit 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1366079, 1733538 and 1835793, which are all the same idea at slightly different weights: cream rosette, teal inside it, grey scatter around. Symmetry order and scale of the medallion vary a little; the underlying arrangement does not.

THE THREE STATES (shown for 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661). Neutral is the soft, layered, translucent version - milky overlaps, a fine interior filigree, the medallion contained well inside the frame. STRESS is loud and unmistakable: the translucency drops away, elements separate into discrete hard blocks, the teal gains area and saturation, and a dark void or a pale radial bloom opens at the exact centre. 1203347 stress cracks its cream ring apart into detached teal-and-cream blocks around a black star-shaped hole. 1243682 stress goes from fine filigree to a big blunt six-point star with a black dot at centre. 1283437 stress replaces the teal core with a whitish pinwheel bloom. 1310661 stress is the most violent - the teal stops being a contained core and floods almost the whole frame, leaving a small cream flower in the middle; figure and ground swap. RECOVERY, on all four seeds, is a near-return to neutral. At 256px I can find the differences (recovery on 1203347 has more teal chips out in the ring, 1310661 recovery has a heavier cream collar than neutral) but they are small. Functionally this work has two states you can see and a third you have to hunt for.

AT 120px. The centre-versus-scatter idea survives completely; every tile still reads as a medallion on black with confetti around it. What does not survive is the interior filigree - the fine radial detail inside the rosettes on 1203347, 1243682, 1835793 and 1985692 turns to mush and those tiles are then separated only by overall lightness. The six middle-weight seeds converge: at browse size 1203347, 1283437 and 1733538 are close to interchangeable. The two extremes stay distinct and read well small (1310661, 1475115 as bold teal discs; 1991107 as a pale slab with a hole). 1446330 at 120px is close to an empty tile - it reads as a rendering failure rather than as a quiet token. The small teal chips on 1561509 and 1283437 shrink to specks that look like dust on the screen rather than drawing. In the state sheet at 120px, stress is obvious on all four seeds; neutral versus recovery is genuinely hard to call on 1203347 and 1243682.

CRAFT NOTES. Edge clipping is everywhere but is clearly intentional and works - it makes the scatter feel like part of a larger field. The bright cream at full opacity against near-black gives real punch. Where translucent cream stacks on translucent cream (1985692, 1366079, 1991107) contrast collapses and the surrounding scatter disappears into the mass. No element looks broken or misplaced; the weakness is distributional, not technical.
